content.text: In Bangladesh, the limited access to conventional payment platforms, such as Stripe, presents a significant challenge for digital creators seeking to sell their products internationally. Without a viable solution, creators are forced to rely on manual payment processing or local payment methods, resulting in delayed payments, lost revenue, and a disjointed customer experience. For one Bangladeshi creator, this situation was about to change with the deployment of a custom-built, blockchain-based payment stack using Cloudflare infrastructure. With a focus on infrastructure sovereignty and independence, this stack aimed to overcome the limitations imposed by Stripe and enable seamless international payments for digital products.
The Situation Before the Stack

The creator, who wished to remain anonymous, was selling digital products, including ebooks and courses, to international clients. However, the lack of access to Stripe and other conventional payment platforms made it difficult to process payments in a timely and efficient manner. As a result, the creator was forced to rely on manual payment processing, which not only delayed payments but also increased the risk of lost revenue and a negative customer experience.
Why Conventional Options Had Already Failed

The creator had already attempted to use various conventional payment platforms, but none of them were available or restricted in Bangladesh. This led to a situation where the creator was unable to process payments, resulting in delayed payments and lost revenue. Furthermore, the lack of infrastructure sovereignty meant that the creator was dependent on these platforms, which could change their terms and conditions at any time, affecting the creator's business.
The Infrastructure That Was Deployed

To overcome this challenge, the creator decided to deploy a custom-built, blockchain-based payment stack using Cloudflare infrastructure. This stack included GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, Google Drive for file delivery, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. The stack was designed to provide infrastructure sovereignty and independence, enabling the creator to process payments without relying on conventional payment platforms.
Blockchain-based payments enable secure and transparent transactions, overcoming the limitations imposed by conventional payment platforms.
What Happened After Going Live

Creators in Ethiopia, Cameroon, Tanzania, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Iran, and the Philippines face a compounded challenge: not only are conventional payment platforms unavailable or severely limited, but local banking infrastructure may add additional friction to receiving international transfers through alternative channels. Crypto payments remove this layer entirely. A seller in Addis Ababa and a seller in Amsterdam receive USDT transactions through the same NOWPayments infrastructure, at the same speed, with the same 0.5% fee. The blockchain has no knowledge of which country a wallet is located in. The webhook fires to both backends identically. The delivery email sends from the same Resend or Gmail account. Geographic neutrality is not a feature that was added — it is the fundamental property of how blockchains work.
The Lessons That Apply to Your Situation

The creator's experience highlights the importance of infrastructure sovereignty and independence in the digital economy. By deploying a custom-built, blockchain-based payment stack using Cloudflare infrastructure, the creator was able to overcome the limitations imposed by conventional payment platforms and focus on growing their business. This lesson applies to digital creators in Bangladesh and other countries where conventional payment platforms are restricted or unavailable.
